insertions.wikitext: A possible identification concerns Mary Anderson. A 2007 RootsChat research post reproduces a 18 June 1908 Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriage entry for Alexander Elder, full-age bachelor farmer of Gortreaghy, whose father is recorded as Robert Elder, farmer. Alexander married Mary Anderson, full-age spinster of Gortreaghy, daughter of Neil Anderson; witnesses were Robert Anderson and Margaret Elder.<ref>RootsChat, Elder, Murdoch & McMeekin Families; [https://www.rootschat.com/forum/index.php?topic=214109.0 record].</ref> The entry is not yet an inspected original, so it is a secondary-source lead rather than final evidence. It is nevertheless a new, specific parent-bearing record for the Gortreaghy Elder household and gives a testable route for determining whether the Alexander Elder on the Rasharkin Second Presbyterian memorial was a son of the Robert Elder who later occupied Alexander Glasgow's Lisnagaver lot. That identity chain remains unproved. The identification remains uncertain.
insertions.identity_assessment: Mary Anderson-47673 is Neal Anderson-47669's Gortereghy sister, aged 37 in 1901, and daughter of Neal Anderson-41446 and Elizabeth Crawford. The 1908 bride is Mary Anderson of Gortereaghy, daughter of Neil Anderson; the 1911 wife Mary is aged 44. The common locality and father, with an age-compatible birth estimate of 1864, strongly support this candidate. The three-year difference in the 1911 age and absent spouse attachment are not exclusions. insertions.identity_assessment: The printed marriage register adds John Bruce’s trade of smith, independently of the generic OPR index. Glasgow-3143 is already supported as Marion who married the Edinburgh weaver William Calder in June 1686; that established life segment is not transferred into this 1684 event. Bruce-6113 represents Sir John Bruce of Kinross with the 1687 Christian Leslie marriage, whereas Bruce-3507 has only a speculative Clackmannan son whose own profile explicitly leaves his baptism/parentage open. Neither inspected family supplies this smith-and-Marion couple. Different spouses alone are not exclusions; keep both candidate husbands qualified and the events separate. insertions.wikitext: A possible identification concerns Sarah McCaughern. The 1911 Gortereghy census browse records Sarah McCaughern, aged 82, as head of household with Matilda Mulholland, 52, and Caroline McCaughern, 47, recorded as daughters; Sara Jane McCaughern, 45, and Jas Alex McCaughern, 43, are also listed as children, with Geo Mulholland, 14, as grandson. insertions.identity_assessment: Original 1901/1911 returns prove household continuity, widowhood and Derry birth. The original 1851 Sarah Dysart/John McCaughern marriage supplies locality and generation compatibility; Sarah’s minor status conflicts slightly with an 1829 birth inferred from census age 82, so treat ages as reported and retain Dysart-1893 as probable-compatible rather than matched. No census names husband or maiden surname. If the identity is retained, carry John McCaughern-23 as the same uncertain father hypothesis across the proved siblings; their mother relationship to documentary Sarah is certain. insertions.wikitext: A possible identification concerns Robert Elder. The reproduced Third Portglenone Presbyterian marriage list records Robert Elder, full-age bachelor labourer of Ballymoney, marrying Jane Adams McCaughey, full-age spinster of Garvaghey, on 13 July 1887. The source is a secondary transcription and the original register remains to be inspected. The identification remains uncertain.
insertions.identity_assessment: Robert Elder-3949, son of James Elder and Mary Jane McAughin, was born on 21 September 1858 in the local Gortereghy/Ballymoney family. Identification remains unproved without an original marital-status and address chain. James Elder-3946 is a possible father identity for the marriage clause, but that identity and mother Mary Jane are not proved by the 1887 marriage alone. insertions.wikitext: A possible identification concerns Robert Elder. The published headstone transcription for Rasharkin Second Presbyterian Church records a memorial erected by Alexander Elder of Gortrickey to his father Robert Elder, his mother Jane, and his sisters and brothers. It also records Alexander Elder's death on 5 January 1943.<ref>Rasharkin Second Presbyterian Church headstones; [https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/graveyard.html record].</ref> This is a new direct memorial transcription for the catalogue's parentage study, not a Glasgow record and not proof that the Elder family was related to Alexander Glasgow. Its value is locality context: Gortrickey/Gortereghy is the townland where the Glasgow family appears in the 1837–1838 Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism entries. The memorial supplies a named Elder household for future comparison with the later Robert Elder who occupied Alexander Glasgow's former Lisnagaver lot; identity between those Elder references remains unproved. The identification remains uncertain.
insertions.identity_assessment: Elder-7144 remains compatible for the living 1901 father of Alex/Robert/Eliza/Margaretta; its 1827 birth is tree-derived and differs from reported age 65, so retain uncertainty. Do not exclude Elder-7251 globally from Sarah’s 1893 father clause merely because a father can be deceased at marriage. Sarah and Isaac’s father occurrences remain unproved bridges to the 1901 family. The original 1881 Jane birth proves Robert/Jane Calderwood as a parental couple, not the mother identity of all later siblings. insertions.wikitext: A possible identification concerns Margaret Glasgow. Betham’s abstract of Archibald Glasgow of Rathmalton, clerk, whose will was dated April 1673, names his wife Elizabeth, Thomas Glasgow as eldest son and Margaret as only daughter. Margaret’s husband is an unnamed Cairns, and Thomas Cairns is her son.<ref>Archibald Glasgow’s will abstract names his eldest son Thomas; [https://catalogue.nli.ie/Record/vtls000540633 record].</ref> Betham’s pre-destruction derivative abstract was inspected, not the original will. The father–son statement is explicit; identification of the son with [[Glasgow-3556]] remains strongly probable, with no residence or estate bridge. Elizabeth’s surname remains provisional. The identification remains uncertain.
insertions.identity_assessment: Betham’s manuscript pedigree of Archibald Glasgow, Rathmalton clerk, whose will was dated April 1673, expressly names Margaret as his only daughter, married to an unnamed Cairns, with son Thomas Cairns. This proves the documentary father–daughter pair. Glasgow-3186, wife of George Lyell in South Leith in 1633, remains a candidate because a later Cairns marriage is possible, but no marriage or household bridge is proved. The Scottish Archibald profile identity remains qualified; no profile father upgrade follows. Glasgow-1523’s cited 1638 baptism names father William Glasgow, a concrete father conflict; its guessed 1642 death is not evidence. Working-model review, 16 October 2026: Select William Glasgow-3075, the Leith mealmaker, as the low-confidence working father of Margaret Glasgow-3186, indexed marrying George Lyell at South Leith on 28 November 1633. William’s household is documented at Leith, with a proposed 10 July 1610 local marriage and a son Archibald baptised in 1618, securely linked to the adult mealmaker by the 1639 apprenticeship and 1647 service of heir. A daughter marrying in 1633 fits that established household generation. Shared surname, the same parish and a coherent marriage/child generation favour this named household over a newly invented father. No source calls Margaret his daughter. Her circa-1610 birth remains an inherited estimate and supplies no independent evidence of William’s paternity. Retain the strongest specific alternative: Betham’s pedigree of Archibald Glasgow, Rathmalton clerk, whose will was dated April 1673, names Margaret as his only daughter, wife of an unnamed Cairns and mother of Thomas Cairns. The documentary father–daughter relationship is explicit, but identifying that Margaret with Glasgow-3186 remains unproved. A first Lyell marriage in 1633 permits a later Cairns marriage. The preferred William placement avoids requiring that unproved Scottish–Irish identity and remarriage. It also avoids tension with the probable identification of Archibald Glasgow-1101 as the child baptised in Glasgow in 1614 and the 1635 graduate: that child would be an implausible father of a 1633 bride. This is a ranking consideration, not an exclusion: the Scottish identity is unproved, and a baptism is not necessarily an infant’s birth. The new uncertain William field must not be used as a concrete father conflict to reject the Rathmalton candidate. A different South Leith Glasgow father also remains possible. No mother is selected: Catherine Fraith/Fraser’s 1610 bride identity and Christian Scot’s separate Glasgow household remain qualified. William’s testament names Archibald as lawful son and sole executor, not only child; omission of Margaret neither excludes her nor proves kinship. insertions.identity_assessment: The Kirknewton 12 May 1666 Agnes–James Swan occurrence is not merged with the 8 July 1670 Agnes–Patrik Paul occurrence. Swan-736’s represented family is with Alisone Peibles at Elie, married 1631; the wife’s estimated 1663 death permits a later marriage, so the different earlier spouse is not an exclusion. Its child William Swan has no inspected connection to this Agnes or Kirknewton. Longformacus 1666 Agnas–William Anderson is not combined into a remarriage biography with the Kirknewton Swan/Paul events. Anderson-3493’s cited 1632 Alloa baptism names William Andersone/Margarat Crokit, proving that child’s record parentage, not that of the Longformacus groom. Agnes candidates’ indexed natal households are compared individually; no Longformacus family clause bridges them. The 1670 Agnes–Patrik Paul event remains separate from the 1666 Agnes–James Swan event, even in the same parish. The supplied births index identifies local Agnes in 1677 to Alexander, which is a different child-record assertion and does not name the 1670 bride’s father. Unrestricted Patrick/Patrik Paul searches from the first audit found no surviving historical match; no new bridge appeared in the cross-record review. The 1681 Carstairs bride is a separate identity question from Agnes with Swan in 1666, Paul in 1670 and Anderson at Longformacus. Inveresk siblings Agnes (1634), Thomas (1637) and Marion (1642) have the indexed father Thomas, but no inspected Carstairs clause joins either Agnes or the 1679 Thomas bridegroom to that family. Thomson-263 has an Edinburgh Peirie household; its attached children add no Carstairs bridge and no dated competing household at 1681. Retain it as a weaker compatible spouse lead.
